The RadWaitingBar class acts to transfer events to and from the RadWaitingBarElement class. RadWaitingBarElement can be nested in other telerik controls.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the RadTextBoxTextRangeProvider class with the specified owner provider, start, and end positions.
member.param: The owner provider of the text range.
The start position of the text range.
The end position of the text range.
member.remarks:
Start and End indicate caret positions and not char indices from within the text. 0 1 2 3 4 - caret positions a b c d - characters 0 1 2 3 - char indices
If there is a range "abcd", then start = 0, end = 4. If start = 1 and end = 3, the range is "bc".

member.name: P:Telerik.WinControls.FileDialogs.RadOpenFileDialogForm.Filter
member.summary: Gets or sets the file name filter string that determines which files are displayed in the dialog. The filter string contains filter pairs separated by the pipe character, where each pair consists of a description and pattern. For example: "Text files (*.txt)|*.txt|All files (*.*)|*.*"

member.summary: Gets or sets the index of the currently selected filter in the file type drop-down list. The index is one-based, where 1 corresponds to the first filter in the string. Setting this to 0 or an invalid index will select the first available filter.

member.name: P:Telerik.WinControls.FileDialogs.RadOpenFileDialogForm.MultiSelect

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the read-only checkbox in the dialog is currently checked. When checked, this typically indicates that the selected file should be opened in read-only mode. This property only has an effect when is set to true.

member.name: P:Telerik.WinControls.FileDialogs.RadOpenFileDialogForm.ShowReadOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the dialog displays a read-only checkbox. When enabled, users can indicate their intention to open the selected file in read-only mode. The state of this checkbox can be accessed through the property.

member.name: T:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.ITaskbarList4
member.summary: Implements 4 ITaskbarList interfaces that are used to control the taskbar items. ITaskbarList: Exposes methods that control the taskbar. It allows you to dynamically add, remove, and activate items on the taskbar. ITaskbarList2: Extends the ITaskbarList interface by exposing a method to mark a window as a full-screen display. ITaskbarList3: Extends ITaskbarList2 by exposing methods that support the unified launching and switching taskbar button functionality added in Windows 7. This functionality includes thumbnail representations and switch targets based on individual tabs in a tabbed application, thumbnail toolbars, notification and status overlays, and progress indicators. ITaskbarList4: Extends ITaskbarList3 by providing a method that allows the caller to control two property values for the tab thumbnail and peek feature.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.STPFLAG.STPF_NONE
member.summary: No specific property values are specified. The default behavior is used: the tab window provides a thumbnail and peek image, either live or static as appropriate.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.STPFLAG.STPF_USEAPPTHUMBNAILALWAYS
member.summary: Always use the thumbnail provided by the main application frame window rather than a thumbnail provided by the individual tab window. Do not combine this value with ; doing so will result in an error.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.STPFLAG.STPF_USEAPPTHUMBNAILWHENACTIVE
member.summary: When the application tab is active and a live representation of its window is available, use the main application's frame window thumbnail. At other times, use the tab window thumbnail. Do not combine this value with ; doing so will result in an error.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.STPFLAG.STPF_USEAPPPEEKALWAYS
member.summary: Always use the peek image provided by the main application frame window rather than a peek image provided by the individual tab window. Do not combine this value with ; doing so will result in an error.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.STPFLAG.STPF_USEAPPPEEKWHENACTIVE
member.summary: When the application tab is active and a live representation of its window is available, show the main application frame in the peek feature. At other times, use the tab window. Do not combine this value with ; doing so will result in an error.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.TBPFLAG.TBPF_NOPROGRESS
member.summary: Stops displaying progress and returns the button to its normal state. Call this method with this flag to dismiss the progress bar when the operation is complete or canceled.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.TBPFLAG.TBPF_INDETERMINATE
member.summary: The progress indicator does not grow in size, but cycles repeatedly along the length of the taskbar button. This indicates activity without specifying what proportion of the progress is complete. Progress is taking place, but there is no prediction as to how long the operation will take.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.TBPFLAG.TBPF_NORMAL
member.summary: The progress indicator grows in size from left to right in proportion to the estimated amount of the operation completed. This is a determinate progress indicator; a prediction is being made as to the duration of the operation.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.TBPFLAG.TBPF_ERROR
member.summary: The progress indicator turns red to show that an error has occurred in one of the windows that is broadcasting progress. This is a determinate state. If the progress indicator is in the indeterminate state, it switches to a red determinate display of a generic percentage not indicative of actual progress.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.Core.TBPFLAG.TBPF_PAUSED
member.summary: The progress indicator turns yellow to show that progress is currently stopped in one of the windows but can be resumed by the user. No error condition exists and nothing is preventing the progress from continuing. This is a determinate state. If the progress indicator is in the indeterminate state, it switches to a yellow determinate display of a generic percentage not indicative of actual progress.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.TaskbarProgressState.NoProgress
member.summary: Stops displaying progress and returns the button to its normal state. Use this flag to dismiss the progress bar when the operation is complete or canceled.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.TaskbarProgressState.Indeterminate
member.summary: The progress indicator does not grow in size, but cycles repeatedly along the length of the taskbar button. This indicates activity without specifying what proportion of the progress is complete. Progress is taking place, but there is no prediction as to how long the operation will take.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.TaskbarProgressState.Normal
member.summary: The green progress indicator grows in size from left to right in proportion to the estimated amount of the operation completed. This is a determinate progress indicator; a prediction is being made as to the duration of the operation.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.TaskbarProgressState.Error
member.summary: The progress indicator turns red to show that an error has occurred in one of the windows that is broadcasting progress. This is a determinate state. If the progress indicator is in the indeterminate state, it switches to a red determinate display of a generic percentage not indicative of actual progress.

member.name: F:Telerik.WinControls.Taskbar.TaskbarProgressState.Paused
member.summary: The progress indicator turns yellow to show that progress is currently stopped in one of the windows but can be resumed by the user. No error condition exists and nothing is preventing the progress from continuing. This is a determinate state. If the progress indicator is in the indeterminate state, it switches to a yellow determinate display of a generic percentage not indicative of actual progress.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.Ascii
member.summary: Represents the ASCII encodation. Allowed characters include double digit numerics and all values from the ASCII table.
member.remarks: The double digit numerics use 4 bits. The ASCII values in the 0-127 range use 8 bits. The ASCII values in 128-255 range use 16 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.C40
member.summary: Represents the C40 encodation. Used primarily for upper-case alphanumerics.
member.remarks: The upper-case alphanumeric characters use 5.33 bits. The lower-case and special characters use 10.66 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.Text
member.summary: Represents the Text encodation. Used primarily for lower-case alphanumerics.
member.remarks: The lower-case alphanumeric characters use 5.33 bits. The upper-case and special characters use 10.66 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.X12
member.summary: Represents the X12 encodation. Uses the characters from ANSI X12 EDI data set.
member.remarks: Each character takes 5.33 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.Edifact
member.summary: Represents the EDIFACT encodation. Used to encode ASCII values in the 32-94 range.
member.remarks: Each character takes 6 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.Base256
member.summary: Represents the Base256 encodation. Used to encode characters in the whole ASCII range.
member.remarks: Each character takes 8 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Barcode.Symbology.Encodation.AsciiGS1
member.summary: Represents the ASCII GS1 encodation. Used to encode FNC1 characters in the ASCII range.
